correctness.rationale: A prime divides the product/LCM quotient exactly when at least two entries are multiples. For L=k+1, this holds always for p<=L/2, never for p>=L, and on L-p residues for the intermediate primes. CRT gives independent Bernoullis. Shifting by any candidate period times T_k/p isolates the p-indicator, forcing divisibility by p; the empty product case has period 1. The parity product vanishes iff 3p=2L, hence iff p=2 and k=2. The PNT integrals of t^(-1)-1 and (t^(-1)-1)(2-t^(-1)) give log 2-1/2 and 3 log 2-2, and the constant small-prime count adds 1/2 to the mean coefficient. Bernoulli third absolute moments are bounded by the variances, so Berry–Esseen divides the total third moment by sigma^3 and gives O(1/sigma). For parity, g(t)=log|3-2/t|=log 3+log|t-2/3|-log t integrates to -(2/3)log 2. With x=L and eta=exp(-c sqrt(log x)/3), truncation to log eta makes total variation O(sqrt(log x)); Stieltjes summation with the quoted PNT error makes its weighted prime-sum error o(x/log x). The truncated integral converges in L^1 and 1<=|3p-2x| for integers x>=4, so the O(eta x+1) affected integers contribute an error at most O((eta x+1)log x)=o(x/log x). This proves the magnitude asymptotic without an unsupported uniform-prime approximation at the singularity.
residual_risks: The enumeration checks finite cases only. The Gaussian statement takes uniform sampling over the exact period before k grows; the asymptotic for the absolute bias does not assert an eventual sign.

value.rationale: A natural arithmetic statistic has both ordinary Gaussian fluctuations and a substantially smaller alternating bias, with explicit constants. The Gaussian part is a routine distributional mechanism once the prime support is identified, but the log bias measures arithmetic cancellation not captured by the Gaussian law or the finite census alone; the singular prime sum is a worthwhile additional estimate for this established quotient family.
residual_risks: No result for short intervals of n, for simultaneous growth beyond full-period sampling, or for the sign of the bias.
